title: Don’t Miss Saturn in All its Glory This Weekend - Nautilus
gist: Saturn reaches opposition on the night of October 3–4, appearing at its brightest of the year about 20 degrees above the southeastern horizon, with the Orionids meteor shower following later in October.

insights.claim: Saturn will be in opposition to Earth on the night of Saturday, October 3 into early Sunday October 4, with Earth directly between Saturn and the sun.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.locator: October’s biggest star is actually a planet.

insights.claim: At opposition Saturn will be at its brightest of the year and visible about 20 degrees above the horizon in the southeastern sky.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.quote: the ringed planet will be at its brightest this year
insights.locator: October’s biggest star is actually a planet.

insights.claim: There are at least two notable celestial events in October: Saturn's opposition and the Orionids meteor shower later in the month.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.locator: There are at least two celestial events

insights.claim: Nautilus recommends observers prepare for October's night sky with a blanket and a thermos of hot chocolate as cooler fall nights arrive.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
